Using the fact that $2=\frac{2}{1},$ we can write the expression as

$$
\frac{2}{1}+\frac{3-x}{1-x}.
$$

 

In order to add the two fractions, we need them to have a common denominator. So, we put both fractions over a common denominator of $1-x$ by multiplying the top and bottom of the first fraction by $1-x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{1}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{1-x}{1-x}\cdot \frac{2}{1}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{2(1-x)}{1-x}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we add the fractions and simplify the result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(1-x)}{1-x}+\frac{3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{2(1-x)+(3-x)}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{2-2x+3-x}{1-x} & = \\ \frac{5-3x}{1-x}\end{aligned}
$$
